newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK property prices seen soft to mid-yr - BEA's Li.
newsitem.headline: HK property prices seen soft to mid-yr - BEA's Li.

text.p: Hong Kong property prices are likely to soften until the middle of the year, Bank of East Asia Ltd's new chairman David Li said on Tuesday.
"I think property prices are on the high side...I think prices will soften until around June and July," Li told reporters following the bank's annual general meeting.

The bank's deputy general manager and chief financial officer, Daniel Wan, earlier said mortgage applications in April had slowed compared to the first quarter after the government announced measures to cool down property prices.
In a bid to speed up the flow of new supply to the market, the government last month extended the presale period for unfinished flats to 15 months before completion from 12 months.

It also required developers to put uncompleted flats on to the market within six months of receiving government approval for presales, and to release the flats in batches of at least 20 percent of the total number of approved units.
Earlier in January, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) recommended capping luxury home mortgages at 60 percent of a property's value from the original 70 percent.
Li called on the HKMA, the territory's de facto central bank, not to interfere too much in mortgage lending.
